test.title: ESAT Mathematics 1 Calibration Test
research_design_notes: The order alternates accessible, visual, direct and unfamiliar items rather than forming an obvious difficulty ladder.
Six question pairs compare the same underlying skill across different presentations.
Option counts vary from 6 to 8 to support realistic distractors.

questions.question_text_markdown:
A drink contains syrup and water in the ratio \(2:3\). \(150\text{ mL}\) of water is added to \(250\text{ mL}\) of the drink.

What is the new ratio of syrup to water?

solution.title: Turn the original ratio into actual volumes.
steps_markdown: The \(250\text{ mL}\) drink contains \(100\text{ mL}\) syrup and \(150\text{ mL}\) water.
After adding water, the volumes are \(100\text{ mL}\) syrup and \(300\text{ mL}\) water.

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests whether the student treats ratios as quantities rather than adding directly to ratio parts.

distractor_analysis.A: Adds the water but treats the original syrup amount as 200 mL.
distractor_analysis.B: Uses the original total as though it were all water after dilution.
distractor_analysis.E: Adds 150 to the water-side ratio number rather than converting to volumes.
distractor_analysis.F: Reverses or incompletely simplifies the updated quantities.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely added to the ratio directly or ignored that 2:3 describes five equal parts.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely weak ratio-to-quantity modelling rather than a simple arithmetic slip.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Understands ratios but converts between parts and quantities inefficiently.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests a stable misconception about changing one part of a mixture.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Likely caught an initial failure to convert the ratio into actual volumes.

questions.pair_interpretation: Q1 is familiar linear ratio reasoning; Q9 uses proportional powers in an unfamiliar algebraic context.

What is \(\angle ACB\)?

solution.title: Find the angle at the centre first.
steps_markdown: Radii are perpendicular to tangents, so the angles at \(A\) and \(B\) in quadrilateral \(OAPB\) are both \(90^\circ\).
The angle at the circumference subtending the same minor arc is half the angle at the centre.

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests whether the student can chain two circle facts rather than applying one theorem directly.

distractor_analysis.B: Subtracts the tangent angle from 90 degrees.
distractor_analysis.C: Assumes the angle at the circumference equals the angle between tangents.
distractor_analysis.E: Uses half of \(180-20\) or misidentifies the subtended arc.
distractor_analysis.F: Finds the correct central angle but does not halve it.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely applied a single familiar angle rule to the wrong angle.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely lacks a connected map of tangent and circle theorems.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Understands the facts but takes time to decide which auxiliary lines and angle sums matter.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests confusion between central, circumference and tangent angles.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: May indicate the student initially used the major arc and then corrected the subtended arc.

questions.pair_interpretation: Q4 tests 2D theorem selection; Q11 tests spatial Pythagoras plus algebra.

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests exact manipulation and whether the student recognises a conjugate shortcut.

distractor_analysis.B: Finds only half of the numerator difference.
distractor_analysis.D: Doubles the correct result after rationalising both fractions separately.
distractor_analysis.F: Takes the reciprocal of the numerator difference.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely a sign or conjugate-recognition error.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely lacks a reliable exact-surds method.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Can manipulate surds but may be rationalising each term separately and creating excess work.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests an entrenched misconception about conjugates or subtracting surds.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often indicates a recovered sign error.

questions.pair_interpretation: Q2 tests exact calculation; Q10 tests whether the student can abandon exact calculation and estimate efficiently.

questions.question_text_markdown:
The variables \(p,q\) and \(r\) satisfy

\[p=\frac{3q-r}{2q+r}.\]

Which expression gives \(q\) in terms of \(p\) and \(r\)?

solution.title: Clear the fraction before collecting the terms containing q.

questions.diagnostic_value: Separates basic symbolic fluency from later, harder rational-equation work.

distractor_analysis.B: Stops with the denominator \(2p-3\) but loses the required negative sign.
distractor_analysis.D: Changes both signs while collecting terms.
distractor_analysis.E: Adds rather than subtracts the coefficient of \(q\).

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely selected a visually similar sign pattern without checking by substitution.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely has difficulty collecting a variable appearing in both numerator and denominator.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Understands rearrangement but lacks a compact line-by-line method.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests a systematic sign or transposition misconception.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often shows successful checking by substituting the chosen form back into the original equation.

questions.pair_interpretation: Q3 is direct rearrangement; Q12 uses similar manipulation inside a rational equation with domain restrictions.

questions.question_text_markdown:
The table shows the scores obtained by a group of students.

| Score | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Frequency | 2 | 5 | \(x\) | 1 |

The mean score is \(2.5\).

What is \(x\)?

solution.title: Write total score divided by total frequency.

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests whether the student can convert a small data table into an equation.

distractor_analysis.A: Treats the mean as the missing frequency.
distractor_analysis.B: Uses only the known frequencies in the denominator.
distractor_analysis.C: Uses the middle score as the missing frequency.
distractor_analysis.D: Makes a small error in the weighted total.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely used an unweighted mean or ignored that x affects both numerator and denominator.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely a genuine gap in constructing means from frequency tables.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Can model the table but equation setup is not automatic.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests confusion between values and frequencies.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often indicates the student noticed x belongs in both total score and total frequency.

questions.pair_interpretation: Q5 is direct table modelling; Q13 requires reconstructing a histogram before estimating a mean.

questions.question_text_markdown:
The line \(y=2x+5\) touches the curve \(y=x^2-4x+k\) at exactly one point.

What is the value of \(k\)?

solution.title: A tangent gives one repeated solution.
steps_markdown: For exactly one solution, the discriminant is zero.

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests whether the student translates geometric language into an algebraic condition.

distractor_analysis.A: Assumes tangency occurs when k is zero.
distractor_analysis.B: Sets only the constant term to zero.
distractor_analysis.C: Uses the turning-point x-coordinate as k.
distractor_analysis.D: Makes an arithmetic error in the discriminant.
distractor_analysis.G: Drops the coefficient 4 in the discriminant.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely did not translate 'touches' into a repeated-root condition.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Could indicate either a discriminant concept gap or weak simultaneous-equation setup.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Understands the model but method selection is not automatic.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests a misconception about tangency or quadratic roots.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often indicates a recovered sign error in moving the line equation.

questions.question_text_markdown:
A machine produces \(18\) components every \(12\text{ s}\). Each component has mass \(25\text{ g}\).

At what rate does the machine produce mass, in kilograms per minute?

solution.title: Convert the production rate to one minute.
steps_markdown: In \(60\text{ s}\), the machine completes \(60/12=5\) batches.

questions.diagnostic_value: Provides isolated evidence on unit conversion and rate fluency.

distractor_analysis.A: Uses the mass of one 12-second batch and labels it per minute.
distractor_analysis.B: Scales the number of components incorrectly.
distractor_analysis.C: Converts grams to kilograms incorrectly or misses part of the minute scaling.
distractor_analysis.E: Rounds or treats 25 g as 0.025 kg but uses 120 components.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely omitted one conversion or multiplied by 60 rather than dividing by 12.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Accurate but unit conversion is not fluent.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests a systematic seconds-to-minutes or grams-to-kilograms error.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often indicates a final unit check caught an otherwise correct numerical method.

questions.question_text_markdown:
Two different numbers are chosen at random from

\[1,2,3,4,5,6.\]

What is the probability that their product is divisible by \(6\)?
questions.diagnostic_value: Tests systematic enumeration and whether unordered choices are counted correctly.

distractor_analysis.B: Misses some products containing separate factors 2 and 3.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely guessed from divisibility intuition without building the sample space.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely weak systematic listing or confusion over ordered versus unordered outcomes.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Accurate but listing method may be inefficient or poorly organised.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often means a duplicated or omitted pair was found during checking.

questions.pair_interpretation: Q6 tests an unconditional sample space; Q14 tests conditioning the same style of pair-counting.

questions.question_text_markdown:
A quantity \(T\) is directly proportional to \(m^{3/2}\) and inversely proportional to \(\sqrt p\).

The value of \(m\) is increased by \(44\%\), while the value of \(p\) is decreased by \(19\%\).

By what factor is \(T\) multiplied?

solution.title: Write both percentage changes as convenient squares.
steps_markdown: Because \(\sqrt p\) is in the denominator, the total factor is

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests transfer of ratio reasoning into a compact unfamiliar power-law model.

distractor_analysis.A: Uses only the square root of the increase in m.
distractor_analysis.B: Uses the 44% multiplier directly and ignores p.
distractor_analysis.D: Applies the decrease in p in the wrong direction.
distractor_analysis.F: Overcompensates for the inverse square-root factor.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely treated percentage changes additively or ignored the fractional powers.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely a genuine gap in direct/inverse proportion with powers.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Can reason through the structure but lacks fluency with convenient percentage squares.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests a stable misconception about how powers affect proportional changes.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: May indicate the student initially multiplied by 0.9 instead of dividing by it.

questions.pair_interpretation: Correct Q1 but wrong Q9 suggests transfer or powers difficulty rather than basic ratio weakness.

questions.question_text_markdown:
Which is the best estimate of

\[\frac{(3.98)^2\times0.051}{0.198}?\]

solution.title: Round to numbers that preserve the scale.

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests whether the student can choose an efficient approximation instead of attempting exact multiplication.

distractor_analysis.B: Treats the square and denominator cancellation incorrectly.
distractor_analysis.F: Introduces an extra factor of ten.

diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely tried exact arithmetic and lost control of decimal places.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Numerical judgement is sound, but the student may not recognise when estimation is the intended method.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Likely caught a factor-of-ten error by comparing magnitudes.

questions.pair_interpretation: Correct Q2 but slow or wrong Q10 suggests over-reliance on exact methods rather than weak arithmetic.

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests whether 2D Pythagoras knowledge transfers to a 3D algebraic model.

distractor_analysis.A: Uses the diagonal as though it were one edge.
distractor_analysis.B: Finds an incorrect value of x and multiplies consecutive sides.
distractor_analysis.E: Adds rather than multiplies one stage of the dimensions.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely guessed a familiar 3-4-5 result without forming the 3D equation correctly.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Could indicate difficulty integrating geometry and algebra rather than either skill alone.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Strong method but low fluency in expanding or solving the quadratic.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests a misconception about the space-diagonal formula.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often indicates the negative root or volume calculation was checked.

questions.pair_interpretation: Correct Q4 but wrong Q11 suggests difficulty transferring geometry into algebra or 3D, not a broad geometry gap.

questions.question_text_markdown:
A bag contains \(4\) red, \(3\) blue and \(2\) green counters. Two counters are selected at random without replacement.

Given that at least one selected counter is red, what is the probability that both are red?

solution.title: Restrict the sample space to pairs containing at least one red.
steps_markdown: So \(26\) pairs contain at least one red.

questions.diagnostic_value: Separates sample-space counting from understanding of conditional probability.

distractor_analysis.A: Uses the unconditional probability of two red counters.
distractor_analysis.C: Treats the condition as if the first counter is definitely red.
distractor_analysis.E: Approximates from the red proportion without conditioning exactly.
distractor_analysis.F: Uses the number of both-red pairs over 13 rather than 26.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely computed the ordinary probability of two reds and ignored the condition.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Understands conditioning but sample-space counting is inefficient.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests the phrase 'given that' is not changing the student's denominator.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often indicates the denominator was successfully restricted after an initial unconditional calculation.

questions.pair_interpretation: Correct Q6 but wrong Q14 isolates conditional probability as the issue.

solution.title: Combine the fractions after noting the excluded values.

questions.diagnostic_value: Provides harder evidence on algebraic fluency after the direct rearrangement in Q3.

distractor_analysis.B: Reverses the signs of both roots.
distractor_analysis.C: Finds both roots but discards the positive one without reason.
distractor_analysis.D: Finds both roots but discards the negative one without reason.
distractor_analysis.G: Misses the factors of 2 in both roots.
distractor_analysis.H: Assumes the rational form prevents real roots.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely cancelled across a sum or chose denominator restrictions as solutions.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Conceptually secure but manipulation speed is below admissions-test pace.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests an entrenched invalid-cancellation or factorisation habit.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often indicates the student checked roots against the original denominators or recovered a sign error.

questions.pair_interpretation: Correct Q3 but wrong Q12 points to complexity tolerance or fraction manipulation, not basic rearrangement.

questions.question_text_markdown:
From point \(A\), the angle of elevation of the top of a vertical tower is \(30^\circ\). After moving \(20\text{ m}\) directly towards the tower to point \(B\), the angle of elevation is \(60^\circ\).

The ground is horizontal. What is the height of the tower?

solution.title: Use the same height in two tangent equations.
steps_markdown: Let the distance from \(B\) to the tower be \(x\) and the height be \(h\).

questions.diagnostic_value: Tests integrated modelling after isolated algebra, ratio and geometry evidence has already been collected.

distractor_analysis.B: Returns the distance from B to the tower.
distractor_analysis.D: Uses the movement distance as the height.
distractor_analysis.E: Uses 20 m as the nearer horizontal distance.
distractor_analysis.G: Uses the original distance as 30 m but multiplies by \(\sqrt3\).

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely used only one observation point or confused tan 30 with tan 60.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely struggles to turn a verbal geometry context into simultaneous relations.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Good integrated reasoning but model construction is not yet automatic.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests a stable exact-trig or diagram-modelling misconception.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often means the student corrected which distance is x versus x+20.

solution.title: Use the median to reconstruct the missing bar, then estimate the mean.
steps_markdown: The class frequencies are \(12,10h,20,16\), so the total is \(48+10h\).
At \(t=18\), \(8/10\) of the second class has been included, so cumulative frequency is \(12+8h\).

questions.diagnostic_value: Capstone data question that distinguishes simple table fluency from reverse inference and grouped-data reasoning.

distractor_analysis.A: Returns the given median as the mean.
distractor_analysis.B: Uses the midpoint of the overall range or rounds too early.
distractor_analysis.D: Uses an incorrect value of h or class midpoint.

diagnostic_interpretation.fast_wrong: Likely skipped the median reconstruction and guessed from the visual centre.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_wrong: Likely a true gap in frequency density, interpolation or grouped means.
diagnostic_interpretation.slow_correct: Strong statistical reasoning but insufficient speed for a layered data item.
diagnostic_interpretation.high_confidence_wrong: Suggests a stable misconception such as treating bar height as frequency.
diagnostic_interpretation.changed_to_correct: Often indicates the student noticed unequal class widths or corrected the total frequency.

questions.pair_interpretation: Correct Q5 but wrong Q13 indicates difficulty with grouped continuous data or multi-step inference, not basic averages.

paired_diagnostic_design.comparison: familiar ratio mixing versus unfamiliar direct/inverse power scaling

interpretation.q01_only: basic ratio secure; transfer to powers or unfamiliar contexts weak
interpretation.q09_only: possible careless or reading error on the simple item

interpretation.q02_only: over-reliance on exact methods or weak numerical judgement
interpretation.q10_only: approximation sense stronger than exact surd manipulation

paired_diagnostic_design.comparison: direct formula rearrangement versus a rational equation

interpretation.q03_only: basic rearrangement secure; algebraic fractions or complexity tolerance weak
interpretation.q12_only: possible careless sign error on the direct item

paired_diagnostic_design.comparison: 2D theorem selection versus 3D geometry translated into algebra

interpretation.q11_only: circle-theorem knowledge gap rather than broad geometry weakness

paired_diagnostic_design.comparison: direct frequency-table mean versus reverse histogram inference

interpretation.q05_only: grouped data, frequency density or multi-step inference weak
interpretation.q13_only: possible careless setup error on the direct table item

interpretation.q06_only: conditional denominator is the likely gap
interpretation.q14_only: systematic listing or divisibility counting issue

diagnostic_model.scope_note: This calibration diagnoses Mathematics 1 only. Physical reasoning is not scored; it should be reported as not_applicable rather than inferred from mathematical performance.
diagnostic_model.weighted_accuracy_formula: 100 * sum(difficulty_weight * correct) / sum(difficulty_weight) over the score's evidence questions
diagnostic_model.confidence_calibration_formula: 100 - 25 * mean(abs(predicted_probability - correctness)), where confidence 1..5 maps to probabilities 0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,0.95; clamp to 0..100

calculation_accuracy.calculation: 100 * (weighted correct answers not tagged as concept_gap or wrong_method) / weighted attempted answers; use observed error attribution when available, otherwise weighted accuracy

time_management.calculation: 0.65 * mean pace_score_per_question + 0.20 * completion_rate + 0.15 * end_section_completion_rate, where end_section is questions 11-15

consistency.calculation: 100 - 12.5 * unexplained_pair_disagreements - 5 * high_confidence_reversals; clamp to 0..100. A disagreement is not penalised when the harder item is wrong and the pair interpretation identifies a narrower skill.

confidence_calibration.reliability: high if at least 12 confidence ratings, medium if 7-11, low if 1-6

reliability_rule.high: at least 4 relevant questions or at least 3 relevant questions with one deliberate pair
reliability_rule.insufficient: 0 relevant questions or more than half the relevant questions skipped

diagnostic_model.overclaiming_guardrail: Never describe a low-reliability score as a stable weakness. Use 'possible weakness' and recommend confirmation with additional questions.

rules_in_priority_order.label: clear_knowledge_gap
rules_in_priority_order.condition: weighted_accuracy <= 40 and relevant_attempted_questions >= 2 and (slow_wrong_count >= 1 or high_confidence_wrong_count >= 1)

rules_in_priority_order.label: inconsistent
rules_in_priority_order.condition: all remaining cases with at least 2 evidence questions

profile_classification_rules.label: Broadly ready
profile_classification_rules.condition: overall_readiness >= 75 and completion_rate >= 0.9 and no high-reliability skill score < 60

profile_classification_rules.label: Strong in familiar problems, weaker in unfamiliar contexts
Needs foundational work
profile_classification_rules.condition: overall_readiness < 45 and knowledge < 50 and at least 4 curriculum tags have weighted_accuracy < 50

strong_but_slow.reason_template: Accuracy is secure, but median response time is above the target range.

fast_but_inaccurate.reason_template: Responses are faster than target but error rate is too high.
fast_but_inaccurate.reassessment_condition: after 40 attempts with at least 80% accuracy

developing.reason_template: Understanding is partial but not yet reliable across contexts.

clear_knowledge_gap.reason_template: Repeated errors indicate a concept or method gap rather than pace alone.
clear_knowledge_gap.reassessment_condition: after completing the topic lesson and 30 practice questions

inconsistent.reason_template: Performance changes substantially across closely related questions.
inconsistent.reassessment_condition: after 2 mixed sets with no repeated error pattern

insufficient_evidence.reason_template: The calibration did not collect enough relevant evidence.
insufficient_evidence.reassessment_condition: after at least 5 additional questions in this skill

strong_and_fast.reason_template: Accuracy and speed are both currently strong.
strong_and_fast.reassessment_condition: reassess in 21 days or after a performance drop

result_page_schema.suggested_retest_date_rule: 7 days for fast-but-inaccurate or strong-but-slow profiles; 10-14 days for developing or clear knowledge gaps; 21 days for broadly ready profiles
result_page_schema.precision_warning: This 15-question calibration provides directional evidence. Low-reliability conclusions must be confirmed with more questions.
